title: World Snooker Masters & Riyadh Season
subtitle: Micro-Detail Lighting Calibration & Ultra-Silent Control
venue: Boulevard Riyadh City, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
broadcaster: Matchroom Sport / Saudi Sports Company (SSC) / Eurosport
role: Lead CCU Engineer & System QC Supervisor
summary: Flawless colorimetry calibration for the high-prestige World Snooker tournament. Demanded zero acoustic noise in arena, ultra-precise baize green color matching, and macro slow-motion ball spin analysis.

specs.replay: EVS XT3 Max with SuperMotion License
specs.cameras: Grass Valley LDX 86N + Sony HDC-4300 Macro Overhead

technicalApproach: Calibrated green baize cloth color balance across all 14 cameras to ensure identical RGB values between tight macro ball shots and wide table views.
Integrated 300fps super slow-motion overhead camera to reveal micro ball collisions and cue contact points.
Engineered ultra-quiet sound isolation and fiber routing to guarantee zero equipment noise reached players.

signalFlow.description: Overhead 4K optical zoom focused on cue tip impact point
Precision Grass Valley OCP-400 paint controllers calibrated against X-Rite ColorChecker
EVS XT3 server continuous buffer capturing 300fps slow-motion cue strikes
Vizrt Trio automated ball telemetry and frame score overlays
Simultaneous international clean feed delivery to Matchroom and SSC

challengesAndSolutions.challenge: Slight hue variance between table spot lights caused the green cloth to appear yellowish on tight pocket cameras.
challengesAndSolutions.solution: Created secondary matrix color presets on Grass Valley OCP panels, selectively shifting yellow-green hue by -4° on pocket cameras.
challengesAndSolutions.impact: Uniform, broadcast-perfect baize green across every single camera angle.

outcomes: Praised by international host directors for the cleanest snooker visual calibration of the season.
Zero technical interruptions throughout the multi-day championship.
improvementReflection: Adding automated robotic micro-jib tracks on overhead positions will allow seamless 360-degree table orbits in future tournaments.
